label: Each thing that can not-be is, at…, from The past is infinite: before every time up… and 1 more
meaning: Bridge (#401): the tertia via's "what can not-be, at some time is not" (STMT-WHAT-CAN-NOT-BE-SOMETIME-IS-NOT) follows from the plenitude principle over an infinite past (STMT-PLENITUDE-OVER-INFINITE-PAST) together with an infinite past (STMT-PAST-IS-INFINITE). For a being that can not-be, the possibility of its not being is realized at some past time; so at some time it is not. The bridge uses only the past time that plenitude supplies, not its being before now.
